statement: Let n = len(stones). On the index set I = {i | 0 <= i < n}, define i ~ j to mean i != j and (stones[i][0] = stones[j][0] or stones[i][1] = stones[j][1]). Let connected be the reflexive-transitive closure of ~ on I, and let c be the number of equivalence classes of connected (equivalently, the number of connected components of the undirected graph on I whose edges are the pairs with i ~ j). The function returns a result r and r = n - c.
preconditions: len(stones) >= 1 and len(stones) <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(stones), len(stones[i]) = 2, 0 <= stones[i][0] <= 10000, and 0 <= stones[i][1] <= 10000; and for every i,j with 0 <= i < j < len(stones), it is not the case that stones[i][0] = stones[j][0] and stones[i][1] = stones[j][1].

statement: The function remove_stones returns a result r on every input satisfying the preconditions; it does not fail (no overflow, out-of-bounds access, or panic).

statement: The function returns a result r. Let m be the nonnegative integer equal to r. There exists a sequence i_1, ..., i_m of distinct indices from {0, ..., len(stones)-1} (empty when m=0) such that for every t with 1 <= t <= m, putting S_t = {i_1, ..., i_{t-1}}, there is an index j with 0 <= j < len(stones), j != i_t, and j not in S_t, satisfying stones[i_t][0] = stones[j][0] or stones[i_t][1] = stones[j][1]. Thus r stones can legally be removed in that order.

statement: The function returns a result r. For every m >= 0 and every sequence i_1, ..., i_m of distinct indices from {0, ..., len(stones)-1} that is legal in the following sense: for each t with 1 <= t <= m, before removing i_t there is an index j with 0 <= j < len(stones), j != i_t, and j not in {i_1, ..., i_{t-1}} such that stones[i_t][0] = stones[j][0] or stones[i_t][1] = stones[j][1]; we have m <= r.

statement: The function returns a result r, and r = len(stones) - 1 if and only if all stones lie in a single connected component: for every i with 0 <= i < len(stones), there exist m >= 0 and indices k_0, ..., k_m in {0, ..., len(stones)-1} such that k_0 = i, k_m = 0, and for every t with 0 <= t < m, stones[k_t][0] = stones[k_{t+1}][0] or stones[k_t][1] = stones[k_{t+1}][1].
